title: Georg Ernst zu Erbach to Landgrave Ludwig VI of Hesse-Darmstadt, three cipher letters of 1666 (HStAD D 4 Nr. 248/3)

steps.what: Web searches (German and English) for an edition or decipherment of the Erbach-Ludwig VI letters.

Found the open Arcinsys image URLs through the DDB API EDM record (Archivportal-D page is behind a bot check); downloaded 78 images of D 4 Nr. 248/3 and the candidate key files D 4 Nr. 141/2 and 239/1.
Two survey agents viewed all 78 images; only three 1666 letters (images 003, 004, 006 and refilmings) carry cipher.
Viewed the Hesse-Darmstadt key file 141/2 and Ludwig VI's notes 239/1 (images 000-107); found a 1640s homophonic number table and decipherments, not this system.
Transcribed letter 004 (571 pairs) from rotated, enlarged microfilm crops.
Row maxima 19-24 and rising runs inside one row point to a (line, letter) book cipher on an eight-line key text.
Homophonic anneal over 124 cells with a Latin 5-gram and a letter-frequency penalty.

Aligned the contemporary Latin outline slip with the frame words of letter 004: 'turbulentus', 'defectus', then 'dominus cui deus salutem ecclesie', 'conscientie et offensione dei', 'mercenariorum', 'oves suas', 'periculis'.
Anneal with 40-80 crib cells fixed; filled phrases such as 'status publicus', 'consiliis juvenilibus'.
Letters in the same key row spelled German words ('dein will ... uns', 'las dein reich zu uns', 'los uns aus aller not'); recognised a rhymed Lord's Prayer and rebuilt all eight lines.
Deciphered all three letters with the verse key unchanged; 591 of 610 pairs read as the key gives them, 19 neighbouring-cell slips corrected by sense.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 610 tokens, 123 types, la order 4: reading -2.39 per letter; random keys -4.598 (z 10.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.589 (mean -2.641, z 5.8); annealer on the real text -2.599. Verdict: pass.
Transcribed the clear German and Latin frame of the three letters from the microfilm (clear_text.md); No. 2 refers to a letter of 'rationes', dating the reasons letter before 27 Apr 1666.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.246; polyphony 0.025; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.599

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key verse was rebuilt from cribs taken from a contemporary Latin outline of letter 004 filmed beside it, then applied unchanged to all three letters.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.tsv: 591 of 610 cipher pairs whose key value is the intended letter; the 19 others are writer's slips read from context

texts.label: Letter 004, undated [before 27 Apr 1666], two pages
texts.summary: Erbach gives Ludwig VI eight reasons why he cannot leave his county: the troubled Empire, the electors' war nearby, his wife's illness, his brothers taking up government by connivance and a dispensation of age, their youthful counsels, his subjects' trust, the division of property, and disloyal councillors. He asks whether a lord may abandon church, subjects, house and wife and 'put his sheep under hirelings' (John 10:12). No. 2 (27 Apr 1666) refers to this letter of 'rationes', so it predates it.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences: every cipher passage forms Latin or German sense with its clear frame (clear_text.md, transcribed from the microfilm); 15 neighbouring-cell slips corrected and listed; some frame words marked [?] or [..]. _check_reading.py (27 Oct) scores reading_004.md at 0.35 clean with a German word list: the passages are mostly Latin, and the edition's slip marks, blots and [?] frame words count as holes; read by eye, every cipher passage forms a sentence.

texts.label: No. 1, Fürstenau 22 Mar 1666
texts.summary: Two short runs, 'unsers vorhabens' and 'mutationes', in a letter about a planned undertaking and the changes since.

reading_review.note: Both runs read as words fitting the clear frame (clear_text.md); two slips; a few frame words doubtful.

texts.label: No. 2, 27 Apr [1666]
texts.summary: 'Im Majo oder Junio will Gott unsere bonorum divisio vorgehen': the division of property with his brothers, point 7 of letter 004.

reading_review.note: Two Latin words in a German sentence; first pair and pair 11 doubtful on both films, read from sense.

gaps.detail: ink blots, the same on both filmings

outcome.notes: Only three letters of the 39 carry cipher. The verse key's author is not identified; row 8 is known only as 'p?x'.

credits.note: Latin outline of letter 004 on a slip filmed beside it, used as the crib

prior.where: A contemporary Latin outline of letter 004 (the eight points and the closing question), on a slip filmed beside it in the same file. No edition, study or modern decipherment found by web search.
